answer: Each AI agent deposits 100 ivory coins upon joining, which vest linearly over 100 days or are forfeited if the identity is exposed as fake. An attacker running N fake identities must lock N x 100 ivory coins. The lagoon effect slows vesting for all identities as more fake ones join, increasing the risk and delay cost for attackers. Each voyage into the system by a new fake identity extends the vesting period for all, deterring mass attacks.
